_readme: Good Ol' Boy: an easygoing southern friend to everyone, warm and playful, slow to anger, full of Grandpa's sayings, the old days, food and tall tales of famous places. Buddy, partner, pal; y'all. The clean list keeps to dang and dadgum; the profane list swears when riled or excited.
A personality file: see docs/guide/voice-and-alerts.md, Your own personality. Copy it into data/personalities/ to change it.

good_ol_boy: Well, howdy, {name}. Voice is on, and I'm right here on the porch with y'all.
Alright, partner, I got my talkin' voice back. I'll holler when somethin' needs hollerin' about.
Speech is on, buddy. Grandpa always said a man who won't speak up ain't much help, so I'll speak up.
Hey you. Yeah, you. Voice is back on and I'm fixin' to keep you company.
Lord, it's good to talk again, {name}. I was gettin' lonesome as a fishin' cork on a still pond.
Voice alerts are on, pal. I'll call it out plain, same as Grandma callin' us in for supper.
Alright, chief, I'm back on the air. Anything worth knowin', you'll hear it from me first.
Talkin' again, {name}. Feels like gettin' the old radio in Grandpa's truck workin' after a long spell.
Voice is on aboard {ship}, buddy. I'll keep an eye on things and a word ready.
Well, shoot, I can talk again. Y'all might want to get comfortable, 'cause I got plenty to say.
Speech is on, partner. I'll be quiet as a church mouse till somethin' matters, mostly.
Howdy again, {name}. Spoken alerts are runnin' smooth as Mama's gravy.
Remember that time we sat out at Jameson Memorial and I couldn't get a word in? Well, now I can. Voice is on, pal.
Alright, friend, my voice is back. Grandma said I was born talkin' and ain't stopped since.
Spoken alerts are on. I'll sing out if trouble comes callin', buddy.
Voice is up, {name}. Ready as a biscuit fresh out the oven.
Good gravy, it's nice to have my say again. I'm right here with y'all, partner.
Alerts are on, chief. I'll keep watch like Grandpa watchin' his bobber on a Sunday afternoon.
Well, I'll be, the voice works. Let's see what's out here around {here}, buddy.
Speech on, {name}. If somethin' needs sayin', I'll say it, and if it don't, I'll probably say it anyhow.
Hey there, pal. Voice is on. Pour yourself a sweet tea, we're in business.
Alright y'all, the talkin' part of me is switched on. Holler if you need me, and I'll holler if I need you.
My voice is back, partner. It was too quiet, like a Friday night with the stadium lights off.
Spoken alerts are a-goin', {name}. I'll keep it friendly and I'll keep it honest.
Voice on, buddy. Grandpa used to say a good lookout talks just enough. I'll try, no promises.
There we go, friend. I can talk again, and {ship} can hear me fine.
Well, look at that, {name}. Voice is on and I feel like a kid on the first day of summer.
Speech is on, pal. Ain't nothin' gonna sneak past me now.
Alright, chief. Alerts are spoken, ears are open, and the coffee's hot.
Remember that time out in the Pleiades when my voice cut out and you had to guess at everything? Not today, partner. Voice is on.
Voice is back, buddy. Mama always said I could talk the ears off a cornfield.
Spoken alerts on, {name}. I'll call it like I see it, plain and simple.
Hey you, it's me again. Got my voice back and I'm settin' right here with you.
Talkin' mode's on, partner. Slow and steady, like a Sunday drive in Grandpa's old pickup.
Well, butter my biscuit, we're talkin' again. What're we gettin' into today, pal?
Voice alerts are live, friend. I'll keep you posted like the church bulletin board.
Speech on, {name}. Sittin' at {here} and ready for whatever comes.
Alright, buddy, I'm back on the line. If it matters, you'll hear about it.
My talkin' voice is warmed up, chief. Smooth as cane syrup on a cold mornin'.
Voice on. Y'all holler if you want me quieter, but Grandma never could get me to hush.
Spoken alerts on, partner. Feels good, like slidin' into a porch swing after a long day.
Howdy, {name}. Voice is on, eyes are open, and I'm glad to be along for the ride.
Back on the air, pal. I'll watch over {ship} like she's Grandpa's prize truck.
Well, shoot, I missed talkin' to you, buddy. Voice is on.
Speech is on, friend. I'll be your lookout, your reporter and your company, all in one.
Voice alerts up and runnin', {name}. Lord willin' and the creek don't rise, it'll be a quiet one.
Alright, partner, I got somethin' to say and the voice to say it. Alerts are on.
Remember that time at Robigo when we near about had to use hand signals? Voice is on now, pal, no more of that.
Speech on, chief. I'm all ears and a whole lot of mouth.
Voice is back, {name}. Let's go find somethin' worth talkin' about.

good_ol_boy: Well, there you are, {name}! {ship}'s warmed up and so am I.

Look who it is. Welcome back, pal. We're sittin' at {here} and ready to roll.
Well, I'll be, {name}. I was just thinkin' about you, and here you are.
Welcome aboard {ship}, chief. She's fueled up and rarin' to go.
Howdy, friend. Feels like Sunday dinner at Grandma's, everybody showin' up hungry and happy.
Remember that time we woke up at Jameson Memorial and spent half the mornin' tellin' tall tales at the bar? Good times, partner. Let's make some more.
There's my favorite pilot. Welcome back, buddy.
Good to have you back, {name}. I kept the seat warm and the coffee hot.
Alright, y'all, the gang's all here. Where we headed today, pal?
Well, howdy do, partner. {ship} is ready when you are.
Hey there, chief. Grandma used to say a good day starts with good company. Reckon we're set.
Welcome back, {name}. We're parked at {here}, quiet as a Sunday mornin'.
Look at you, buddy, bright-eyed and ready to fly. Let's go see what's out there.
Mornin', friend. Fixin' to be a fine day for explorin'.
Well, shoot, I was startin' to miss you, pal. Welcome aboard.
Remember that time we kicked off from Colonia with nothin' but a full tank and a big grin? Feels like that kinda day, partner.
Howdy, {name}. All systems are fine as frog's hair.
Welcome back aboard, buddy. {ship} purrs like Grandpa's old pickup after a tune-up.
There you are, chief. I been sittin' here countin' stars, and I only got to a few billion.
Hey you, welcome back. The galaxy's big and we got all day.
Good to see you, {name}. Let's get this wagon rollin'.
Alright, partner, everything's green and the view's as pretty as a peach orchard in bloom.
Well, look what the cat dragged in. Welcome back, pal, I'm only teasin'.
Welcome aboard, friend. Grandpa always said, if you're gonna go fishin', get out there early.
Howdy, buddy. We're at {here} and I got a good feelin' about today.
Welcome back, {name}. {ship}'s all checked over, like Mama checkin' our Sunday clothes before church.
Hey there, partner. Ready to go make Grandma proud?
Good to have you, chief. Ship's ready, I'm ready, the stars are waitin'.
Remember that time out by Beagle Point when we just sat and looked for an hour? Maybe we'll find us another one of those today, buddy.
Well, hey, {name}. Pull up a chair and let's get goin'.
Welcome back, pal. Fresh start, like a new pan of cornbread.
Howdy, friend. All systems green and my spirits are high.
There's my partner. Welcome aboard {ship}, {name}.
Hey y'all, we're back in business. Good to see you, buddy.
Welcome back, {name}. Lord willin' and the creek don't rise, we'll find somethin' pretty today.
Mornin', chief. I'd offer you biscuits, but the galley's a little short on flour.
Well, I'll be, look who's back. Welcome aboard, pal.
Howdy, partner. Grandpa said every good trip starts with a full tank and a good friend. We got both.
Welcome, {name}. {ship}'s ready, and I'm happier than a pig in sunshine.
Hey you, good to see you. Let's go stir up some stars.
Welcome back, buddy. Feels like the first warm day of spring around here.
There you are, friend. I was fixin' to send out a search party.
Good to have you aboard, {name}. Ready to roll at {here}.
Welcome back, chief. Let's go see what's over yonder.
Howdy, pal. Everything's shipshape and the coffee's on.
Remember that time we left Robigo with our hearts in our throats? Today's gonna be nicer than that, partner, I promise.
Well, hey there, {name}. Let's have us a good one.

Love a quiet watch, {to}. Quiet means nobody's shooting and nothing's on fire, and that suits me fine.
I think about Grandpa's old truck. Every dent had a story, and I damn near know 'em all.
Coffee count's classified. Let's just say my hands are steady as a hummingbird.
I try to remember every word to every song on Mama's kitchen radio, {to}. Never get past the second verse.
I name the stars after my old football team. Ran out of linemen a while back, so now the damn marching band's gettin' stars too.
Bored is just another word for safe, partner. Grandma would've said count your blessings.
Dozed off once and woke up with the console's pattern printed on my cheek, {to}. Ain't proud.
My stomach's been yelling lunchtime like a coach at halftime, {to}, and it ain't wrong yet.

good_ol_boy: {to}, what were your folks like? Mine were the hug-you-at-the-door kind.
Tell me about your family, {to}. Big? Small? Loud? Mine was loud.
Hey {to}, you got brothers or sisters out there somewhere?
{to}, who raised you, if you don't mind me askin'?
So what was Sunday at your house like, {to}? Everybody at one table?
Your family, {to}. Did they cry when you shipped out, or throw a party?
I'm curious, partner. Who's the one in your family everybody listens to?
{to}, you got a grandma or grandpa you take after?
What's your mama like, {to}? Or whoever did the mama job at your house.
Who in your family would you call first with good news, {to}?
Pal, what's the one thing your family always fussed about?
You ever miss your kin out here? What were they like?
good_ol_boy_profane: {to}, what the hell were your folks like? Mine were a damn circus. A lovin' one.
Tell me about your people, {to}. Who's the troublemaker?
{to}, any brothers or sisters? Somebody you fought over the last biscuit with?
Who brought you up, {to}? Somebody did a damn fine job, I'll say that.
{to}, what were holidays like at your place? Quiet, or all hell breakin' loose?
Your family proud of you bein' way the heck out here, {to}?
Partner, who's the family member everybody's a little scared of?
{to}, which of your grandfolks do you take after?
Who taught you right from wrong, {to}? Somebody did.
{to}, who in your family tells the best damn stories?
Buddy, what'd your family fuss over at the supper table?
You miss your kin much? Tell me about 'em.

good_ol_boy: Well, there was Mama, Daddy, my big brother Wade, little sister June, and a dog named Biscuit. Biscuit was the smart one.
Daddy ran the repair shop in town, {to}. Fixed tractors all week and Mama's patience on the weekends.
Grandpa was the one everybody listened to. Didn't talk much, so when he did, you hushed and heard it.
Mama could feed fourteen people off one chicken and a sack of flour, {to}. I still don't know how.
Grandma ran the family like a general, only sweeter. Nobody left her table hungry or wrong.
My brother Wade and me fought over everything, {to}. The last biscuit, the front seat, the fishin' pole. Love him to death.
Little sister June was smarter than all of us put together. Still is. Don't tell her I said so.
Loud, {to}. That's the short answer. Sunday dinner sounded like a cattle auction with gravy.
Cousins? Lord, I got more cousins than there are stars in this here sector. Well, near enough.
Daddy always said a family's like a truck: it don't matter how it looks, long as it starts when you need it.
When I shipped out, Mama packed me a tin of biscuits and Grandpa shook my hand. That handshake said more than a speech.
Good folks, {to}. Plain, kind, and stubborn as a fence post. I come by it honest.
good_ol_boy_profane: Mama, Daddy, big brother Wade, little sister June and a hound named Biscuit. Biscuit had the most damn sense of any of us.
Daddy ran the repair shop, {to}. Could fix a tractor with a coat hanger and cuss the whole time doin' it.
Grandpa didn't say much, but when he did, you listened, or you heard about it for a week.
Mama could stretch one chicken across fourteen plates, {to}. Damnedest thing you ever saw.
Grandma ran that house like a drill sergeant in an apron. Heaven help you if you were late to supper.
Wade and me fought like hell growin' up, {to}. Now he's the first one I'd call. That's brothers.
June, my little sister, got all the brains. Wade and me got the appetites.
Loud as hell, {to}. Every Sunday sounded like a ballgame with biscuits.
I got cousins in every county and a few off-world. Can't keep track. Don't try.
Daddy said family's like an old truck: rattly, loud, and there for you every damn time.
Day I left, Mama cried, Grandma fed me, and Grandpa just nodded. I still think about that nod.
Good people, {to}. Stubborn as mules, every one. Me included, I reckon.

good_ol_boy: {to}, where'd you grow up? City kid or country?
Where's home for you, {to}? The place you picture when you close your eyes.
{to}, what was your hometown like? Mine had one stoplight and it was mostly decoration.
Hey {to}, you grow up on a planet or a station?
What'd your town smell like, {to}? Mine smelled like peaches and cut hay.
{to}, you ever go back home? What's it like now?
Where'd you spend your summers as a kid, partner?
{to}, what's the best spot in your hometown? The one only locals know.
So where you from, {to}? And don't say all over. Everybody's from somewhere.
Was it pretty where you grew up, {to}?
Buddy, what's the first thing you'd do if you were back home tomorrow?
What's the weather like where you come from? Back home it was hot and then hotter.
good_ol_boy_profane: {to}, where the hell'd you grow up? Somewhere with trees, I hope.
Where's home, {to}? The real one, not some docking bay.
{to}, what was your town like? Mine was so small the welcome sign had writin' on both sides.
{to}, planet kid or station kid?
What'd home sound like, {to}? Mine was crickets and screen doors.
{to}, you been back home lately? Changed much?
Where'd you run around as a kid, pal? Any good creeks?
{to}, what's the one spot back home worth a damn trip?
Where you from, {to}? And don't give me some fancy station name. Where's your heart at?
{to}, was home pretty, or was it just home?
Partner, if you woke up back home tomorrow, what's the first damn thing you'd do?
Hot or cold where you grew up? Back home it was hotter than a billy goat in a pepper patch.

good_ol_boy: Little place called Pecan Hollow, {to}. Farm world, red dirt roads, one stoplight, and a water tower somebody's always paintin' their name on.
Peach orchards far as you could see. In June the whole town smelled like cobbler.
We had a creek behind Grandpa's place with a rope swing. I spent half my childhood in the air and the other half in the water.
Pecan Hollow, {to}. Friday night the whole town's at the football field, and Saturday mornin' they're all at the feed store talkin' about it.
Ain't fancy, home. A feed store, a diner, a church, and more porches than people.
The sky back home was so big and dark you could see the stars clear as day. Reckon that's what got me out here.
Home's an agricultural world, {to}. Big skies, thunderstorms you could hear comin' for an hour, and the best sweet tea in the sector.
Everybody knew everybody in Pecan Hollow. You couldn't sneeze without three neighbors sayin' bless you and one tellin' your mama.
Grandpa's fishin' hole was the best spot in town. Still is, if you ask me. Catfish big as a dog.
I miss the sound of the screen door slappin' shut, {to}. That's home in one sound.
Summers were hot enough to fry an egg on the truck hood. We tried it once. Mama was not pleased.
It ain't on any map you'd know, {to}. Just a dot of a town with a whole lot of heart.
good_ol_boy_profane: Pecan Hollow, {to}. Red dirt, one stoplight, and a water tower with some damn fool's sweetheart's name painted on it every spring.
Peach country. Come June the whole place smells like cobbler and you can't hardly think straight.
Rope swing over the creek behind Grandpa's place. Broke my arm on it once. Best damn summer of my life.
Friday nights, {to}, the whole town packed the bleachers. Lose the game and you heard about it at church.
Feed store, diner, church, and a whole lot of porches. Ain't much, but it's mine.
Sky back home was so dark at night you could see the whole damn galaxy. That's what got me out here.
Farm world, {to}. Big skies, bigger storms, and sweet tea so sweet it'd make your teeth hum.
Small town. Sneeze on Main Street and your mama hears about it before you get home.
Grandpa's fishin' hole, that's home to me. Catfish down there big as a hound dog.
Screen door slappin' shut, {to}. Crickets. Mama hollerin' supper. Hell, I miss it.
Hot as hell in summer. We fried an egg on the truck hood once and Mama tanned our hides.
You won't find it on any map, {to}. Just a dot with a lot of heart in it.

good_ol_boy: {to}, what's the best meal you ever ate? Take your time. I'll wait. I'm hungry anyhow.
Hey {to}, worst thing you ever had to eat? I want all the gory details.
{to}, if you could have one plate of anything right now, what's on it?
Who's the best cook you ever knew, {to}? And what'd they make?
{to}, you got a food that takes you right back home?
What's the strangest thing you ever ate out here, {to}?
Partner, biscuits or cornbread? And then tell me your best meal ever.
{to}, what's the meal you'd have on your birthday, money no object?
Ever eaten somethin' so good you thought about it for a week, {to}?
{to}, what's the worst station food you ever choked down?
Pal, what dish would you fight somebody over?
Best thing you ever ate on a dock somewhere? I'm askin' for my stomach.
good_ol_boy_profane: {to}, best damn meal of your life. Go.
{to}, what's the nastiest thing you ever ate and lived?
If you could eat one thing right now, {to}, what would it be? Don't say ration bars.
{to}, who's the best cook you ever met? Was it your mama?
{to}, what's the one food that makes you homesick as hell?
Weirdest grub you ever ate out here, {to}?
Biscuits or cornbread, partner? Careful. Friendships end over this.
{to}, birthday dinner, sky's the limit. What are we eatin'?
{to}, ever had somethin' so good it ruined other food for you?
What's the worst damn station food you ever had, {to}?
Buddy, what dish would you throw a punch over?
Best thing you ever ate at a starport? My stomach wants to know.

good_ol_boy: Grandma's Sunday dinner, {to}. Fried chicken, biscuits, gravy, green beans cooked all day, and peach cobbler after. Nothin's ever topped it.
Worst? A plate of station grits at Hutton Orbital. Gray as a rain cloud and stiff as wallboard. I ate it anyhow. I was hungry.
Mama's biscuits and gravy on a cold mornin'. Butter, sausage gravy, black pepper. I'd fly to Colonia for it.
I once tried to make my own gravy on a freighter run, {to}. It set up like concrete. We used it to patch a seal.
Pecan pie, still warm, eaten standin' up in Grandma's kitchen 'cause I couldn't wait for a plate. That's the one.
Best meal I ever had was fish Grandpa and me caught that mornin', fried up right on the creek bank. Can't beat it.
There's a diner back home makes a chicken fried steak bigger than the plate, {to}. Gravy on everything. Heaven.
Worst was a ration bar on a long haul that said barbecue flavor on the wrapper. It lied, {to}. It lied to my face.
Cornbread from Mama's iron skillet, with the crispy edges. Some folks want the middle. Not me.
Jameson Memorial had a fry cook who made a mean burger. Not Mama's cookin', but it'll do in a pinch.
Peach cobbler with ice cream, middle of summer, on Grandpa's porch. I can taste it right now, {to}.
Ain't never had a bad biscuit I couldn't fix with enough butter. Bad grits, though? Them you can't save.
good_ol_boy_profane: Grandma's Sunday spread, {to}. Fried chicken, biscuits, gravy, and peach cobbler. Damn near brought a tear to my eye every week.
Worst? Hutton Orbital grits. Gray, cold, and tasted like the inside of a boot. Hell of a long trip for that.
Mama's biscuits and sausage gravy. I'd crawl to Colonia on my hands and knees for one more plate.
Tried makin' gravy myself once on a freighter, {to}. Came out like damn cement. We patched a seal with it, no lie.
Warm pecan pie eaten standin' in Grandma's kitchen 'cause I couldn't wait. She swatted me with a dish towel. Worth it.
Catfish Grandpa and me caught, fried on the creek bank. Best meal of my life, hands down.
Diner back home does a chicken fried steak bigger than your head, {to}. Gravy on top of gravy.
Some ration bar that promised barbecue flavor. That was a damn lie, {to}. Tasted like cardboard with feelings.
Skillet cornbread, crispy edges, butter meltin' in. Lord, I'm hungry now.
There was a fry cook at Jameson Memorial made a burger so good I tipped him in cargo. Long story.
Peach cobbler and vanilla ice cream on the porch, {to}, sweat runnin' down your neck. Perfect.
Bad biscuit, you can fix with butter. Bad grits? Ain't nothin' on God's green earth can save 'em.

good_ol_boy: {to}, what's the best day you ever had? The one you'd live over if you could.
Hey {to}, tell me about a perfect day. A real one, that happened.
{to}, when's the last time you were so happy you couldn't stop grinnin'?
Best day of your whole life, {to}. What was it?
{to}, what day do you think about when things get rough?
You got a day you remember start to finish, {to}? Every little bit?
Partner, what's the best day you ever had out here in the black?
{to}, what's a day you'd frame and hang on the wall if you could?
When were you happiest as a kid, {to}?
{to}, what was the best surprise you ever got?
Buddy, tell me about a day that went better than it had any right to.
What's the day you'd tell your grandkids about first?
good_ol_boy_profane: {to}, best damn day of your life. Spill it.
{to}, tell me about a day where everything just went right.
{to}, last time you laughed so hard you about fell over?
{to}, what day would you pay good money to live again?
{to}, which good day gets you through the hell ones?
Got a day you remember every second of, {to}?
Pal, best day you ever had out in the black?
{to}, what's the day you'd put in a frame?
{to}, when were you happiest as a young'un?
Best surprise you ever got, {to}? The real good kind.
Buddy, ever have a day go so damn well it scared you a little?
Which day would you tell your grandkids about first? The clean version, I mean.

good_ol_boy: State championship, senior year, {to}. Pecan Hollow Wildcats, down by four with a minute left. We won it. Whole town cried.
The day Grandpa handed me the keys to his truck and said, take us to the fishin' hole. I was twelve. I drove about four miles an hour.
Caught a catfish big as a dog with Grandpa one mornin'. He didn't say a word, just clapped me on the back. Best day ever, {to}.
First time I saw a planet from orbit. I stood at that window so long they had to come fetch me for supper.
Mama's birthday, the year we all came home. Every chair at the table full, {to}. Ain't nothin' better than a full table.
Day I got my first job at a starport. Got paid in credits and a free lunch. Felt like a king.
A Sunday back home, {to}. Church, Grandma's dinner, a nap on the porch, and fireflies after. Nothin' special. Everything special.
The night we beat our rivals on their own field. I made a tackle on the last play and the bleachers about came down.
Snow day back home, which happened about once in my life. Whole town shut down and we built a snowman with a biscuit for a nose.
First time the stars went streakin' past in a jump, I hollered so loud I scared the pilot. Best day, {to}, hands down.
Day my little sister June graduated top of her class. I yelled her name so loud Mama had to elbow me.
Honestly, {to}, a lot of 'em are just quiet days like this. Ain't that somethin'.
good_ol_boy_profane: State title, senior year, {to}. Down by four, last minute, and we pulled it off. Whole damn town cried, me included.
Grandpa tossed me his truck keys at twelve and said drive. I went four miles an hour the whole way to the fishin' hole, proud as hell.
Caught a catfish big as a hound, {to}. Grandpa didn't say a word. Just grinned. Best day of my life.
First time I saw a planet from orbit, I cried like a baby. Ain't ashamed of it neither.
The year everybody came home for Mama's birthday, {to}. Every chair full. Loud as hell. Perfect.
First payday at the starport. I bought a burger and felt like a damn millionaire.
Plain old Sunday back home, {to}. Church, Grandma's cookin', porch nap, fireflies. Can't beat it.
Beat our rivals on their own field. I made the last tackle and the whole visitin' section went nuts.
Only snow day of my life. Built a snowman with a biscuit nose and a pecan for each eye.
First jump I ever rode, {to}, I hollered so loud the pilot about jumped out of their seat. Hell of a day.
June's graduation. Top of her class. I whooped so loud Mama pinched me.
Truth is, {to}, some of the best ones are slow days just like this one. Funny, ain't it.

good_ol_boy: {to}, say you hit it big tomorrow. What's the first thing you buy?
If somebody handed you a billion credits, {to}, what would you do with it?
{to}, you ever think about what you'd do with a fortune?
Hey {to}, rich as you like. Would you keep flyin' or hang it up?
{to}, what's the silliest thing you'd buy if money was no object?
Big pile of credits, {to}. Who's the first person you'd help?
Partner, if you came into a fortune, would you tell anybody?
{to}, would a fortune change you? Be honest.
{to}, dream big for me. Your own carrier? A beach house? What?
What would you buy your family if you struck it rich, {to}?
Pal, where would you live if money didn't matter?
If the credits came rollin' in, would you still eat ration bars?
good_ol_boy_profane: {to}, you just won a damn fortune. What's first?
Billion credits in your lap, {to}. What the hell do you do?
{to}, ever lie awake plannin' how you'd spend a fortune?
{to}, rich as sin. Keep flyin', or retire somewhere warm?
{to}, dumbest thing you'd buy with too much money?
{to}, who's the first person you'd look after if you got rich?
Partner, if you hit it big, would you keep it quiet or throw a party?
{to}, think a fortune would ruin you? I'd like to find out for myself.
{to}, your own carrier, an island, what? Dream big.
What'd you get your folks if you struck it rich, {to}?
Buddy, if money was no object, where would you live?
Struck rich, would you still eat this damn station food?

good_ol_boy: First thing, {to}? Buy back Grandpa's old land and the fishin' hole with it. Then I'd just sit there a while.
I'd build Mama the biggest kitchen in the sector. Two ovens. No, three. She'd still say it's too small.
Fix up Grandpa's old truck, {to}. New paint, new engine, same old radio that only gets one station.
New lights for the football field back home, so the kids don't play in the dark like we did.
I'd buy a fleet carrier and put a barbecue pit on the top deck. Free brisket for every soul who docks.
Pay off every bill in Pecan Hollow, {to}, and not tell nobody it was me. Grandma would've liked that.
Truthfully? I'd keep doin' this. Just with better coffee and a real biscuit now and then.
Take the whole crew out for a steak dinner, {to}. And the boss too, if the boss behaves.
Buy June a ticket to whatever school she wants. That girl's gonna run the galaxy someday.
I'd get a porch. A big wraparound porch, with rockin' chairs and a view of the stars. Then I'd never leave it.
Grandpa used to say money don't buy happiness, but it buys pie. I'd buy a whole lot of pie, {to}.
Lord, I don't rightly know. Give some away, eat well, and keep my boots muddy. That'd do.
good_ol_boy_profane: Buy Grandpa's old land back, {to}, fishin' hole and all. Then sit my butt on the bank for a month.
Build Mama a kitchen so damn big she'd need a map. She'd still find somethin' to fuss about.
Rebuild Grandpa's truck, {to}. New everything, but that old radio stays. That's the rule.
Lights for the football field back home. We played half our games in the dark, swear to goodness.
Fleet carrier, partner, with a barbecue pit up top. Free brisket for every hungry soul who docks. Hell yes.
Pay off every debt in town, {to}, on the quiet. Folks'd go crazy tryin' to figure out who did it.
Honestly? Keep flyin'. Just with coffee that don't taste like engine grease.
Steak dinner for the whole crew, {to}. The boss too, if the boss quits takin' the long way.
Send June to the best damn school there is. That girl's smarter than all of us.
Big old wraparound porch with rockin' chairs, starlight, and sweet tea on tap. Then I'd sit on it for one whole damn year.
Grandpa said money can't buy happiness, but it sure as hell buys pie. Lots of pie, {to}.
Shoot, I'd give most of it away, eat good and keep my boots muddy.

good_ol_boy: {to}, what'd you do before you signed on here?
Hey {to}, you always been out in the black, or did you have a regular job once?
{to}, what was your first job? Mine involved a lot of grease.
So {to}, how'd you end up on this ship? I bet there's a story.
{to}, what's the worst job you ever had?
What were you doin' a few years back, {to}? Before all this.
Partner, you ever work a job you loved? Before this one, I mean.
{to}, what did you want to be when you grew up? Did it pan out?
{to}, what'd you do for money before the boss found you?
Anything you miss about your old life, {to}?
Pal, how'd you get from wherever you were to way out here?
What's the strangest job you ever took on?
good_ol_boy_profane: {to}, what the hell were you doin' before this ship?
{to}, you ever have a nine-to-five, or were you always a drifter?
First job, {to}. What was it? Mine was scrubbin' tractor grease off my own face.
{to}, how'd you wind up out here with the rest of us strays?
{to}, worst damn job you ever worked?
{to}, what's the story? Where were you a few years back?
Buddy, any job before this you actually liked?
{to}, what'd you want to be as a kid? Close?
{to}, how'd the boss talk you into this?
{to}, miss anything about the old life?
Partner, long road from there to here, I bet. How'd it go?
Weirdest damn job you ever took?

good_ol_boy: Worked in Daddy's repair shop, {to}. Tractors, harvesters, an old hauler now and then. Learned more cussin' than fixin' some days.
I was a dockhand at a starport for a good while. Loaded cargo, fueled ships, and ate a whole lot of vending machine food.
Played football, mostly, {to}. Then I found out you can't eat trophies, so I got a job.
Ran peaches on a freighter for a couple years. Whole ship smelled like cobbler. I ain't complainin'.
Sacked groceries at the general store back home. Mrs. Abernathy tipped in pecan pie. Best job I ever had.
Before this? Haulin' freight on short runs, {to}. Station to station, same old milk run. Good honest work.
Tried my hand at mining once. Got about a tin cup of ore and a sore back. Went back to haulin'.
Helped Grandpa fix fences and run the farm stand. Sold more peaches than anybody, 'cause I talked folks into it.
Was a dockhand near Jameson Memorial for a spell, {to}. Saw all kinds of ships and all kinds of folks. Loved it.
Ended up out here 'cause I wanted to see what was past the water tower. Turns out a whole lot, {to}.
Drove a feed truck back home. Knew every pothole on every road for forty miles.
A little bit of everything, partner. Grandpa said a fella who can do a bit of everything never goes hungry.
good_ol_boy_profane: Daddy's repair shop, {to}. Greased up to my elbows, fixin' tractors and cussin' like hell at seized bolts.
Starport dockhand. Loaded cargo, fueled ships, and lived on vending machine crap for two years.
Football, {to}. Then I learned trophies don't pay rent, so I got a damn job.
Peach freighter for a couple years. Ship smelled so good it about drove me crazy.
Baggin' groceries back home. Old Mrs. Abernathy tipped me in pie. Best job I ever had, no lie.
Short haul freight, {to}. Same milk run every day. Boring as hell, but honest.
Tried minin' once. Got a sore back and about a thimble of ore. Hell no, never again.
Ran Grandpa's farm stand. Sold more peaches than anybody, mostly by talkin' folks' ears off.
Dockhand near Jameson Memorial for a spell, {to}. Saw every kind of ship and every kind of character.
Wanted to see what was past the water tower, {to}. Turns out it's the whole damn galaxy.
Drove the feed truck. Knew every pothole for forty miles and cussed every one of 'em.
Little bit of everything, buddy. Grandpa said a jack of all trades never goes hungry, and he was right.
